descriptionChirho: The proper name Titus (Greek Τίτος), referring to Paul's Gentile co-worker and delegate to Corinth and Crete. Consistently rendered across languages as a transliterated proper noun: Spanish 'Títos,' Arabic 'تيطُسَ/تيطُسُ,' Hindi 'तीतुस,' Korean '디도,' Swahili 'Tito.' All case forms (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative) refer to the same individual and represent inflectional variation rather than semantic distinction.

A variant proper name Titius (Greek Τίτιος), likely referring to Titius Justus (Acts 18:7), a different individual from Paul's companion Titus. Distinguished in transliteration: Spanish 'Títios,' Hindi 'तीतियुस,' Arabic 'تِيتُوسَ,' Korean '디디오,' Swahili 'Titio.' The distinct transliterations across multiple languages confirm this is a separate personal name from Titus/Τίτος.
